**STEP 1 — Scene:** A breakfast tray with dry muesli, milk, a cup of tea or coffee, a small bowl of orange-colored fruit, and a sealed strawberry yogurt.

**STEP 2 — Vessels:** The cereal bowl appears about 17 cm across: area = 3.14 × 8.5² ≈ **227 cm²**. The fruit dish is about 9 cm across: **64 cm²**. For the drinks and yogurt, I use their approximate internal cross-sections below.

**STEP 3 — Items:** Muesli (oats, raisins, and other cereal pieces), milk, orange-colored fruit in a little juice, strawberry yogurt, and tea or coffee. No visible added sugar or separate sauce.

**STEPS 4–6 — Area, volume, and weight:**

| Item | Area covered | Typical height | Gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Dry muesli | 45% of cereal bowl = 102 cm² | 1.6 cm | 163 ml | 0.34 g/ml | 55 g |
| Fruit and visible juice | 65% of fruit dish = 42 cm² | 2.5 cm | 105 ml | 0.65 g/ml | 68 g |
| Milk | 100% of bottle cross-section ≈ 24 cm² | 7.5 cm | 180 ml | 1.03 g/ml | 185 g |
| Tea or coffee | 100% of cup cross-section ≈ 44 cm² | 4.5 cm | 198 ml | 1.0 g/ml | 198 g |
| Strawberry yogurt | Estimated pot cross-section ≈ 28 cm² | 5.3 cm | 148 ml | 1.03 g/ml | 152 g |

The cereal and fruit coverage totals are respectively **45% and 65% of their own vessels**. Dry muesli uses a lower bulk density than cooked grains because it is a loose, dry mixture. The yogurt is sealed, so its contents and fill level are less certain.

**STEP 7 — Energy:** Muesli ≈ 204 kcal; milk ≈ 93 kcal; fruit ≈ 44 kcal; yogurt ≈ 144 kcal; plain tea or coffee ≈ 2 kcal.

**STEP 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **658 g and 487 kcal**, including beverages, is plausible for the visible tray. The cereal itself is only about 55 g; liquids account for much of the total weight. No unseen additions are included.
